1	"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.
2	
3	Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
4	:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
5	deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
6	event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
7	never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
8	information recorded at the time.
9	
10	Automatic yielding
11	------------------
12	When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
13	keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: a parked blocker (one with no
14	bound task *and* no remaining route) is asked to move onto a free side cell
15	that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot facing a blocker that
16	cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free adjacent cell and replan its
17	(still shortest) route from there. A taskless robot that still carries a
18	remaining route is not parked: it drives that route cell by cell exactly like
19	a task-bound robot, is never pushed onto a side cell for someone else, and if
20	its own next cell is blocked it simply keeps its place and its unconsumed
21	waypoints -- an open side cell changes nothing. Only once such a route is
22	exhausted does the robot become a parked robot and yield by the side-cell
23	rule. A retreat that
24	only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
25	replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
26	blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
27	corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
28	empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Yield moves count as
29	mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
30	completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
31	takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
32	time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
33	purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
34	blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
35	:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
36	map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
37	end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
38	asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
39	made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
40	and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
41	tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
42	blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
43	identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
44	interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
45	reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
46	longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
47	entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
48	or increments one.
49	
50	Initial task ownership
51	----------------------
52	A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
53	with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
54	Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
55	while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
56	still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
57	that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
58	a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
59	therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
60	bound to a completed task. Finished tasks only retain *historical* ownership:
61	their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may already work a
62	new task, and may even be absent from the fleet. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
63	tasks simply wait -- including ones no robot can currently reach -- and are
64	not an ownership error. Conflicts raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot
65	or task involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's
66	objects are left untouched. The same unfinished-task binding rules govern
67	checkpoint loading (which additionally keeps its historical-state checks).
68	
69	Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
70	whether or not the robot is bound to a task. The route omits the robot's
71	current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
72	neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
73	from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
74	Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
75	first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
76	must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
77	lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
78	unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
79	shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
80	or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
81	traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
82	its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
83	point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
84	(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
85	behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.
86	
87	Checkpoint file format
88	----------------------
89	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
90	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
91	
92	``version``
93	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
94	``grid``
95	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
96	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
97	``tick``
98	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
99	    loading never advance this value.
100	``robots``
101	    List of robot states, each
102	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
103	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
104	    remaining waypoints after ``position``.
105	``tasks``
106	    List of task states, each
107	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
108	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
109	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
110	``replay``
111	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
112	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
113	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
114	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
115	    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
116	    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
117	    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
118	    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
119	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
120	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
121	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
122	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
123	    robot positions.
124	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
125	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
126	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
127	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
128	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
129	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
130	    ``grid``.
131	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
132	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
133	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
134	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
135	    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
136	    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
137	    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
138	    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
139	    all reject the document.
140	
141	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
142	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
143	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
144	
145	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
146	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
147	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
148	mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
149	that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
150	or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
151	states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
152	:class:`ValueError`.
153	
154	A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
155	walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
156	unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
157	the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
158	pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
159	dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
160	and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
161	route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
162	when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
163	empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.
164	
165	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
166	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
167	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
168	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
169	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
170	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
171	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
172	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
173	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
174	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
175	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
176	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
177	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
178	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
179	"""

198	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
199	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
200	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
201	
202	
203	def _as_cell(value: object, description: str) -> Position:
204	    """Validate a user supplied coordinate as a two-integer pair."""
205	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
206	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
207	    if len(value) != 2:
208	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
209	    if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
210	        raise ValueError(f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types")
211	    return value[0], value[1]

214	def _as_pair(value: object, description: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
215	    if (
216	        not isinstance(value, list)
217	        or len(value) != 2
218	        or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
219	    ):
220	        raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
221	    return value[0], value[1]

224	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
225	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
226	
227	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
228	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
229	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
230	
231	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
232	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
233	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
234	      completes anything by itself.
235	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
236	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
237	
238	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
239	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
240	    unreachable one.
241	    """
242	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
243	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
244	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
245	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
246	    if task.dropoff != last:
247	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
248	    return waypoints

251	def _plan_task_route(
252	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
253	) -> list[Position] | None:
254	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
255	
256	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
257	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
258	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
259	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
260	    """
261	    route: list[Position] = []
262	    current = origin
263	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
264	        try:
265	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
266	        except ValueError:
267	            return None
268	        route.extend(leg)
269	        current = waypoint
270	    return route

283	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
284	        self._map_sequence = 0

288	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
289	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]

291	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
292	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):

301	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
302	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
303	        only governs work still in progress:
304	
305	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
306	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
307	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
308	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
309	          collected additionally must have an owner.

312

323	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}

346	            # task is still in progress.
347	            if task.completed:

349	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:

355	                if owner is None:
356	                    raise ValueError(
357	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
358	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
359	                    )
360	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:

363	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
364	                    )

367	    def _validate_initial_routes(grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]) -> None:

374	        identical consecutive waypoints and a first waypoint equal to the

382	        (a route crossing another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is
383	        left to execution: only walkability on the given map is judged. The
384	        check is read-only -- a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole, and the
385	        caller's robot and task objects are never truncated, padded, reordered
386	        or otherwise modified. Checkpoint loading keeps its own, stricter
387	        validation that also covers the task pickup/dropoff rules.
388	        """
389	        for robot in robots:
390	            route = robot.route
391	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
392	                raise ValueError(
393	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
394	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
395	                )
396	            previous = robot.position
397	            for index, cell in enumerate(route):
398	                waypoint = _as_cell(
399	                    cell, f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
400	                )
401	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
402	                    raise ValueError(
403	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
404	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
405	                    )
406	                if index == 0 and waypoint == previous:
407	                    raise ValueError(
408	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 "
409	                        f"{list(waypoint)} is the robot's current cell; the "
410	                        "remaining route must start with the next cell"
411	                    )
412	                if waypoint == previous:
413	                    raise ValueError(
414	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route repeats cell "
415	                        f"{list(waypoint)} at consecutive waypoints "
416	                        f"{index - 1} and {index}"
417	                    )
418	                if (
419	                    abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
420	                    + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
421	                    != 1
422	                ):
423	                    if index == 0:
424	                        segment = (
425	                            f"from its current position {list(previous)} to "
426	                            f"route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
427	                        )
428	                    else:
429	                        segment = (
430	                            f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} "
431	                            f"to waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
432	                        )
433	                    raise ValueError(
434	                        f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently "
435	                        f"{segment}: every step must move one orthogonal cell"
436	                    )
437	                previous = waypoint

443	    def modify_obstacles(
444	        self,
445	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
446	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
447	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
448	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
449	
450	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
451	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
452	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
453	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
454	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
455	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
456	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
457	
458	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
459	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
460	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
461	        distance is accumulated.
462	        """
463	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
464	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
465	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
466	        if conflict:
467	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
468	            raise ValueError(
469	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
470	            )
471	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
472	        for cell in add_cells:
473	            if cell in occupied:
474	                raise ValueError(
475	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
476	                )
477	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
478	
479	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
480	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
481	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
482	        seen: set[Position] = set()
483	        ordered: list[Position] = []
484	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
485	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
486	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
487	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
488	            if position in seen:
489	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
490	                continue
491	            seen.add(position)
492	            ordered.append(position)
493	        return ordered
494	
495	    def _apply_map_change(
496	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
497	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
498	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
499	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
500	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
501	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
502	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
503	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
504	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
505	
506	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
507	        # known to change the map.
508	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
509	        self._map_sequence += 1
510	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
511	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
512	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
513	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
514	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
515	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
516	
517	    def _map_change_record(
518	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
519	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
520	        return {
521	            "type": "map_change",
522	            "tick": self.tick,
523	            "sequence": sequence,
524	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
525	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
526	        }

528	    def _plan_route(
529	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
530	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
531	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
532	
533	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
534	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
535	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
536	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
537	        """
538	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
539	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
540	
541	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
542	        for task in self.tasks.values():
543	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
544	                continue
545	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
546	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
547	                continue
548	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
549	            if route is None:
550	                robot.route = []
551	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
552	            else:
553	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
554	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
555	                robot.route = route
556	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
557	
558	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
559	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
560	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
561	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
562	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
563	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
564	                continue
565	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
566	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
567	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
568	                continue
569	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
570	            if route is None:
571	                robot.route = []
572	                continue
573	            robot.route = route
574	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
575	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

581	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
582	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
583	        cells: set[Position] = set()
584	        for robot in self.robots.values():
585	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
586	                cells.update(robot.route)
587	        return cells
588	
589	    def _safe_side_cells(
590	        self,
591	        robot: Robot,
592	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
593	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
594	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
595	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
596	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
597	
598	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
599	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
600	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
601	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
602	
603	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
604	          skips anything else),
605	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
606	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
607	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
608	          route is excluded), and
609	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
610	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
611	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
612	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
613	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
614	
615	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
616	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
617	        """
618	        blocked = set(forbidden)
619	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
620	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
621	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
622	                continue
623	            yield cell
624	
625	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
626	        self,
627	        blocker: Robot,
628	        requester: Robot,
629	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
630	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
631	    ) -> Position | None:
632	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
633	
634	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
635	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
636	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
637	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
638	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
639	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
640	        """
641	        return next(
642	            self._safe_side_cells(
643	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
644	            ),
645	            None,
646	        )

648	    def _self_sidestep(
649	        self,
650	        robot: Robot,
651	        task: Task | None,
652	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
653	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
654	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
655	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
656	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
657	
658	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
659	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
660	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
661	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
662	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
663	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
664	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
665	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
666	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
667	        """
668	        if task is None or task.completed:
669	            return None
670	        destination = robot.route[0]
671	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
672	        if blocker_id is None:
673	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
674	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
675	        best_length = 0
676	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
677	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
678	        # that order as the tie break.
679	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
680	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
681	            if route is None:
682	                continue
683	            if (
684	                blocker_id is not None
685	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
686	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
687	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
688	                )
689	            ):
690	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
691	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
692	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
693	                continue
694	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
695	                best = (cell, route)
696	                best_length = len(route)
697	        return best
698	
699	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
700	        self,
701	        robot: Robot,
702	        side: Position,
703	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
704	        blocker_id: str,
705	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
706	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
707	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
708	    ) -> bool:
709	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
710	
711	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
712	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
713	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
714	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
715	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
716	        never rejected here.
717	        """
718	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
719	            return False
720	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
721	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
722	            return False
723	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
724	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
725	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
726	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
727	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
728	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
729	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
730	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
731	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
732	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
733	        return not self._can_vacate(
734	            blocker,
735	            robot,
736	            hyp_occupied,
737	            reserved,
738	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
739	            blocked_path,
740	        )
741	
742	    def _can_vacate(
743	        self,
744	        blocker: Robot,
745	        requester: Robot,
746	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
747	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
748	        checking: frozenset[str],
749	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
750	    ) -> bool:
751	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
752	
753	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
754	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
755	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
756	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
757	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
758	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
759	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave check
760	        is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
761	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
762	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
763	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
764	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
765	        the blocker's own route does).
766	        """
767	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
768	            return False
769	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
770	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
771	            return False
772	        if not blocker.route:
773	            if task is not None:
774	                # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
775	                # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
776	                return False
777	            # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
778	            # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
779	            # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
780	            # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
781	            # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
782	            # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
783	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
784	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
785	        ahead = blocker.route[0]
786	        if (
787	            self.grid.traversable(ahead)
788	            and ahead not in occupied
789	            and ahead not in reserved
790	        ):
791	            return True
792	        occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
793	        if (
794	            occupant_id is not None
795	            and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
796	            and occupant_id not in checking
797	        ):
798	            # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
799	            # vacates its cell this same tick.
800	            if self._can_vacate(
801	                self.robots[occupant_id],
802	                requester,
803	                occupied,
804	                reserved,
805	                checking | {blocker.robot_id},
806	                blocked_path,
807	            ):
808	                return True
809	        if task is None:
810	            # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
811	            # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
812	            # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
813	            return False
814	        # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
815	        # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
816	        # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
817	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
818	            blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
819	        ):
820	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
821	                return True
822	        return False
823	
824	    def _update_traffic_waits(
825	        self,
826	        waited: dict[str, str],
827	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
828	    ) -> None:
829	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
830	
831	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
832	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
833	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
834	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
835	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
836	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
837	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
838	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
839	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
840	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
841	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
842	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
843	        """
844	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
845	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
846	        for robot_id in waited:
847	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
848	                continue
849	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
850	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
851	                continue
852	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
853	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
854	                continue
855	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
856	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
857	                continue
858	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
859	            if entry is None:
860	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
861	            else:
862	                surviving[robot_id] = {
863	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
864	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
865	                }
866	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
867	
868	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
869	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
870	
871	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
872	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
873	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
874	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
875	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
876	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
877	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
878	        """
879	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
880	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
881	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
882	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
883	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
884	                continue
885	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
886	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
887	
888	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
889	        return [
890	            {
891	                "robot_id": robot_id,
892	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
893	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
894	            }
895	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
896	        ]

902	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
903	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
904	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
905	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
906	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
907	            for robot in self.robots.values():
908	                if not robot.idle:
909	                    continue
910	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
911	                if route is None:
912	                    continue
913	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
914	            if not choices:
915	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
916	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
917	                continue
918	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
919	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
920	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
921	            robot.route = route
922	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
923	
924	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
925	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
926	        for robot in self.robots.values():
927	            if robot.task_id is None:
928	                continue
929	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
930	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
931	                task.picked_up = True
932	
933	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
934	        self._confirm_pickups()
935	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
936	        self.assign_tasks()

1018	            )

1024	                continue

1030	            "tick": self.tick,
1031	            "moved": moved,
1032	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},

1038	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:

1091	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
1092	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
1093	
1094	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
1095	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
1096	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
1097	        raise :class:`OSError`.
1098	        """
1099	        document = {
1100	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
1101	            "grid": {
1102	                "width": self.grid.width,
1103	                "height": self.grid.height,
1104	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
1105	            },
1106	            "base_grid": {
1107	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
1108	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
1109	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
1110	            },
1111	            "tick": self.tick,
1112	            "robots": [
1113	                {
1114	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
1115	                    "position": list(robot.position),
1116	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
1117	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
1118	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
1119	                }
1120	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
1121	            ],
1122	            "tasks": [
1123	                {
1124	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
1125	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
1126	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
1127	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
1128	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
1129	                    "completed": task.completed,
1130	                }
1131	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
1132	            ],
1133	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
1134	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
1135	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
1136	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
1137	        }
1138	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
1139	
1140	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
1141	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
1142	        try:
1143	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
1144	            try:
1145	                handle.write(payload)
1146	                handle.flush()
1147	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
1148	            finally:
1149	                handle.close()
1150	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
1151	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
1152	        except BaseException:
1153	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
1154	            try:
1155	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
1156	            except OSError:
1157	                pass
1158	            raise

1164	        except OSError:
1165	            return
1166	        try:
1167	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
1168	        except OSError:
1169	            pass
1170	        finally:
1171	            os.close(dir_fd)

1174	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
1175	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
1176	
1177	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
1178	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
1179	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
1180	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
1181	        """
1182	        try:
1183	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1184	                text = handle.read()
1185	        except OSError:
1186	            raise
1187	        try:
1188	            data = json.loads(text)

1190	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc

1193	    @classmethod
1194	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
1195	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
1196	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
1197	
1198	        version = data.get("version")
1199	        if not _is_int(version):
1200	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
1201	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
1202	            raise ValueError(
1203	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
1204	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
1205	            )
1206	
1207	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
1208	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
1209	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
1210	
1211	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1212	        paused: set[str] = set()
1213	        if version == 1:
1214	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
1215	            base_grid = grid
1216	        else:
1217	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
1218	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
1219	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
1220	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)
1221	            if (base_grid.width, base_grid.height) != (grid.width, grid.height):
1222	                raise ValueError("base grid dimensions must match the current grid")
1223	            cls._validate_map_history(base_grid, grid, map_changes)
1224	
1225	        robots: list[Robot] = []
1226	        for record in robot_records:
1227	            position = _as_pair(record["position"], f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position")
1228	            if not grid.traversable(position):
1229	                raise ValueError(
1230	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} position {list(position)} is outside "
1231	                    "the map or inside an obstacle"
1232	                )
1233	            route: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
1234	            previous = position
1235	            for index, cell in enumerate(record["route"]):
1236	                waypoint = _as_pair(
1237	                    cell, f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {index}"
1238	                )
1239	                if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
1240	                    raise ValueError(
1241	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
1242	                        "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
1243	                    )
1244	                if abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0]) + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1]) != 1:
1245	                    raise ValueError(
1246	                        f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
1247	                        f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
1248	                    )
1249	                route.append(waypoint)
1250	                previous = waypoint
1251	            distance = record["distance_travelled"]
1252	            if not _is_int(distance) or distance < 0:
1253	                raise ValueError(
1254	                    f"robot {record['robot_id']!r} distance_travelled must be a "
1255	                    "non-negative integer"
1256	                )
1257	            robots.append(Robot(record["robot_id"], position, route, record["task_id"], distance))
1258	
1259	        tasks: list[Task] = []
1260	        for record in task_records:
1261	            pickup = _as_pair(record["pickup"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} pickup")
1262	            dropoff = _as_pair(record["dropoff"], f"task {record['task_id']!r} dropoff")
1263	            tasks.append(
1264	                Task(
1265	                    record["task_id"],
1266	                    pickup,
1267	                    dropoff,
1268	                    record["assigned_robot"],
1269	                    record["picked_up"],
1270	                    record["completed"],
1271	                )
1272	            )
1273	
1274	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
1275	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
1276	
1277	        # Ownership is judged with the exact rules direct construction uses:
1278	        # mutual bindings for work in progress, historical owners for finished
1279	        # tasks, and a collected task that may never lack its carrier.
1280	        cls._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
1281	        for task in tasks:
1282	            if task.completed and not task.picked_up:
1283	                raise ValueError(
1284	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is completed but never picked up"
1285	                )
1286	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
1287	                # Direct construction never sees a finished task without a
1288	                # historical owner because it cannot create completion itself,
1289	                # but a checkpoint document can spell one, and the running
1290	                # simulator only ever saves picked-up tasks with a carrier.
1291	                raise ValueError(
1292	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
1293	                )
1294	
1295	        cls._validate_paused_state(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id, grid)
1296	        cls._validate_active_task_routes(paused, task_by_id, robot_by_id)
1297	        traffic_waits = cls._load_traffic_waits(data, robot_by_id)
1298	
1299	        replay_change_frames = cls._replay_map_change_frames(replay)
1300	        if replay_change_frames != map_changes:
1301	            raise ValueError("replay map-change frames do not match 'map_changes' history")
1302	
1303	        simulator = cls(grid, robots, tasks)
1304	        simulator.base_grid = base_grid
1305	        simulator.tick = tick
1306	        simulator.replay = copy.deepcopy(replay)
1307	        simulator.map_changes = copy.deepcopy(map_changes)
1308	        simulator._map_sequence = len(map_changes)
1309	        simulator.paused_tasks = set(paused)
1310	        simulator._traffic_waits = traffic_waits

1313	        # alongside the frames so each frame is judged against its contemporary
1314	        # map.
1315	        cls._validate_replay_positions(replay, tick, robot_by_id, base_grid, map_changes)
